Landmark Isomap ordering

Source: R/13_helpers.R
isomap_ordering.Rd

Build a nearest-neighbor graph, calculate geodesic distances to landmarks, and use a landmark embedding coordinate to order samples.

Usage

isomap_ordering(
  X,
  num_neighbors = 15L,
  component = 1L,
  seed = NULL,
  control = NULL
)

Arguments

X

Numeric sample-by-feature matrix.

num_neighbors

Integer nearest-neighbor count; default 15.

component

Positive embedding-coordinate index; default 1.

seed

Optional random seed for landmark selection.

control

Named advanced settings list: embedding_dims = 1 (at least component), num_landmarks = NULL (uses min(1000, nrow(X))), landmark_method = "random" ("kmeans" also supported), keep = "giant", return_full = TRUE, orient_by_pc1 = TRUE, scale01 = TRUE. Giant-component handling retains the largest connected component; full output has NA for excluded samples. Scaling maps scores to [0,1]; orientation aligns their sign with PC1. Inverse-distance stabilization is an internal numerical rule.

Value

A list with t, keep_idx, n_components, embed, landmark_idx, and geodesic_to_landmark.

Examples

set.seed(1)
isomap_ordering(matrix(rnorm(80), 40, 2), num_neighbors = 10, seed = 1)
